cards.html: Supervisor is a small, Python-based process manager. A daemon, supervisord, starts the programs listed in an INI file as its children, restarts them when they die and captures their output. A client, supervisorctl, controls them. It is not an init system: it manages a handful of app processes, usually on a server where systemd (or a container) runs supervisord itself. It is common in older Python and PHP stacks, Laravel queue workers and Docker images.

sudo apt install -y supervisor        # Debian / Ubuntu package (or: pip install supervisor)
systemctl status supervisor           # the package runs supervisord as a systemd service

On Debian and Ubuntu:

PathContents
/etc/supervisor/supervisord.confMain config: the socket, log locations, and an [include] of conf.d
/etc/supervisor/conf.d/*.confOne file per program: put yours here
/var/log/supervisor/supervisord's own log, plus each program's stdout and stderr logs
/var/run/supervisor.sockThe UNIX socket supervisorctl talks to

/etc/supervisor/conf.d/levelup.conf:

[program:levelup]
command=/opt/levelup/server_fastapi/.venv/bin/uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8766
directory=/opt/levelup/server_fastapi
user=levelup
environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED="1",APP_ENV="production"
autostart=true
autorestart=true
startsecs=5
startretries=5
stopsignal=TERM
stopwaitsecs=20
stopasgroup=true
killasgroup=true
redirect_stderr=true
stdout_logfile=/var/log/supervisor/levelup.log
stdout_logfile_maxbytes=20MB
stdout_logfile_backups=5

cards.s: The options that matter, with their defaults
cards.html:
OptionDefaultMeaning
command(required)The program in the foreground; no shell features
directory, usernoneWorking directory; the account to switch to (supervisord must run as root to switch)
environmentnoneKEY="value",KEY2="value", added to supervisord's own environment
autostarttrueStart when supervisord starts
autorestartunexpectedfalse, unexpected (exit code not in exitcodes) or true (always)
exitcodes0The "expected" exit codes for autorestart=unexpected
startsecs1Seconds the program must stay up for the start to count as a success
startretries3Failed start attempts before giving up (FATAL)

cards.s: The options that matter, with their defaults
cards.html:
OptionDefaultMeaning
stopsignal, stopwaitsecsTERM, 10Stop signal, and how long to wait before SIGKILL
stopasgroup, killasgroupfalseSignal the whole process group, so child processes die too
redirect_stderrfalseMerge stderr into stdout (like 2>&1)
stdout_logfileAUTOLog file; AUTO puts a randomly named file in the child log directory
stdout_logfile_maxbytes, _backups50MB, 10Rotation
numprocs, process_name1, %(program_name)sRun N copies; the name must include %(process_num)s when N > 1
priority999Start order (lower starts first, stops last)

cards.s: The options that matter, with their defaults
cards.html:
Two gotchas from the docs:

  • user= only switches the user ID. It doesn't start a login shell, so HOME, USER and anything in the user's profile are not set. Set what the app needs with environment=.
  • Without stopasgroup and killasgroup, programs that spawn children (Gunicorn workers, multiprocessing, Flask in debug mode) can leave orphans behind when stopped. systemd's cgroups avoid this; with Supervisor you turn these on yourself.

StateMeaning
STOPPEDNot running: stopped on request, or never started
STARTINGStarted, still inside the startsecs window
RUNNINGStayed up for startsecs: a successful start
BACKOFFExited too quickly during STARTING; supervisord will retry, waiting longer each time
STOPPINGA stop was requested, waiting for it to exit
EXITEDExited from RUNNING; autorestart decides what happens next
FATALFailed to start startretries times in a row; supervisord gave up
UNKNOWNSupervisor's own error state

The important path: STARTING → (exits within startsecs) → BACKOFF → STARTING → … → FATAL. A program that crashes on start, for example from a missing environment variable, ends in FATAL after a few seconds. A program that crashes after hours goes RUNNING → EXITED → restarted.

CommandDoes
sudo supervisorctl statusEvery program, its state, PID and uptime
start x, stop x, restart xControl one program (all for every program, group:* for a group)
rereadRead the config files again and show what changed; changes nothing
updateApply the changes: start new programs, restart changed ones, remove deleted ones
reloadRestart supervisord itself, which restarts every program
tail -f xFollow a program's stdout (tail -f x stderr for stderr)
signal HUP xSend a signal, for example to make a program reload its config
pid x, availA program's PID; every configured program

CommandDoes
supervisorctl (alone)An interactive shell for the same commands

The classic mistake: you edit a .conf file and run restart x. restart does not read the config again, so nothing changes. The right sequence is reread and then update.

• [group:web] with programs=levelup,worker lets you restart web:* together.
  • [eventlistener:x] sections run programs that receive supervisord events (process state changes, ticks). The superlance package adds ready-made listeners: crashmail emails on crashes, memmon restarts programs that use too much memory, and httpok restarts a program when its health URL stops answering.

An [inet_http_server] section adds a web UI and an XML-RPC API on a TCP port. Anyone who can reach it can stop and start your programs, so if you turn it on, bind it to 127.0.0.1 and set a username and password. The default UNIX socket is safer: access to it is controlled by file permissions.

cards.s: Lab: run the demo under Supervisor (VM, free)
cards.html:
1. sudo systemctl disable --now demo (so port 8000 is free), then sudo apt install -y supervisor.
  2. Write /etc/supervisor/conf.d/demo.conf for the chapter 4 app, modelled on the example above.
  3. sudo supervisorctl reread (it lists demo: available), then sudo supervisorctl update, then status.
  4. curl localhost:8000/crash and watch status: EXITED, then RUNNING again with a new PID.
  5. Break the command path, then reread and update. Watch the program go through BACKOFF to FATAL, and read /var/log/supervisor/supervisord.log to see why.
  6. sudo supervisorctl tail -f demo while you send requests.

1. You edited a program's .conf file and ran restart, but nothing changed. Why, and what should you run?
  2. A program crashes 0.5 seconds after starting, every time. Which state does it end in?
  3. What is the default autorestart, and what does it mean?
  4. Why turn on stopasgroup and killasgroup for Gunicorn?
  5. The app can't find HOME under Supervisor even though user= is set. Why?

🔒 Answers: try the questions first, then tap to show

1: restart doesn't re-read config; run supervisorctl reread then update. 2: FATAL, after startretries attempts through BACKOFF. 3: unexpected: restart only when the exit code isn't in exitcodes (default 0). 4: So stop and kill signals reach the worker processes, not just the master, and no orphans are left. 5: user= only changes the user ID; it doesn't set HOME or other environment variables, so set them with environment=.
